teaching.title: A calendar date
teaching.note: The day number comes first, then the month in the genitive: 5 марта. Do not add в. The written number is enough here; saying ordinal dates is a separate skill.

examples.en: The lesson will be on 5 March.

examples.en: The meeting will be on 12 May.

teaching.title: Month forms
teaching.note: Learn the name and its date form together. Most month names end in -ь and change to -я; май becomes мая. Март, август end in a hard consonant and add -а.

teaching.title: How long?
teaching.note: To say how long an activity lasted, use a time phrase without a preposition. Минута and неделя change to минуту and неделю. Час, день and месяц look unchanged. You may add один or одну to emphasise one.

examples.ru: Я читал час. Я ждал одну минуту.
examples.en: I read for an hour. I waited for one minute.

examples.ru: Я отдыхал день. Я жил в гостинице неделю.
examples.en: I rested for a day. I stayed at a hotel for a week.

examples.ru: Я жил в Москве один месяц.
examples.en: I lived in Moscow for one month.

teaching.title: A start time is different
teaching.note: В два часа tells you when. Час tells you how long. Первого марта is a date; через неделю means a week later. In practice, use the stated length of time, not one of these other meanings. Длился means lasted.

examples.ru: Урок начался в десять и закончился в одиннадцать. Урок длился час.
examples.en: The lesson started at ten and finished at eleven. It lasted an hour.

examples.ru: Я приехал в понедельник и уехал в следующий понедельник. Я жил в гостинице неделю.
examples.en: I arrived on Monday and left the following Monday. I stayed at the hotel for a week.

teaching.title: How long?
teaching.note: To say how long an activity lasted, use a time phrase without a preposition. Минута and неделя change to минуту and неделю. Час, день and месяц look unchanged. You may add один or одну to emphasise one.

examples.en: I lived in Moscow for one month.

teaching.title: A start time is different

teaching.title: How long?
teaching.note: To say how long an activity lasted, use a time phrase without a preposition. Минута and неделя change to минуту and неделю. Час, день and месяц look unchanged. You may add один or одну to emphasise one.

examples.en: I read for an hour. I waited for one minute.

examples.ru: Я отдыхал день. Я жил в гостинице неделю.
examples.en: I rested for a day. I stayed at a hotel for a week.

examples.ru: Я жил в Москве один месяц.
examples.en: I lived in Moscow for one month.

teaching.title: A start time is different
teaching.note: В два часа tells you when. Час tells you how long. Первого марта is a date; через неделю means a week later. In practice, use the stated length of time, not one of these other meanings. Длился means lasted.

examples.ru: Урок начался в десять и закончился в одиннадцать. Урок длился час.
examples.en: The lesson started at ten and finished at eleven. It lasted an hour.

teaching.title: A calendar date
teaching.note: The day number comes first, then the month in the genitive: 5 марта. Do not add в. The written number is enough here; saying ordinal dates is a separate skill.

teaching.title: Month forms
teaching.note: Learn the name and its date form together. Most month names end in -ь and change to -я; май becomes мая. Март, август end in a hard consonant and add -а.

teaching.title: How long?
teaching.note: To say how long an activity lasted, use a time phrase without a preposition. Минута and неделя change to минуту and неделю. Час, день and месяц look unchanged. You may add один or одну to emphasise one.

examples.ru: Я читал час. Я ждал одну минуту.
examples.en: I read for an hour. I waited for one minute.

examples.ru: Я отдыхал день. Я жил в гостинице неделю.
examples.en: I rested for a day. I stayed at a hotel for a week.

examples.ru: Я жил в Москве один месяц.
examples.en: I lived in Moscow for one month.

teaching.title: A start time is different
teaching.note: В два часа tells you when. Час tells you how long. Первого марта is a date; через неделю means a week later. In practice, use the stated length of time, not one of these other meanings. Длился means lasted.

examples.ru: Урок начался в десять и закончился в одиннадцать. Урок длился час.
examples.en: The lesson started at ten and finished at eleven. It lasted an hour.

examples.ru: Я приехал в понедельник и уехал в следующий понедельник. Я жил в гостинице неделю.
examples.en: I arrived on Monday and left the following Monday. I stayed at the hotel for a week.

teaching.note: To say how long an activity lasted, use a time phrase without a preposition. Минута and неделя change to минуту and неделю. Час, день and месяц look unchanged. You may add один or одну to emphasise one.

teaching.note: This is the same case used for location after в and на, but it expresses a different relationship. Compare на работе — at work, and о работе — about work. For these nouns use -е: мама → маме, друг → друге, семья → семье, книга → книге, музыка → музыке, спорт → спорте.

teaching.title: The topic of a conversation
teaching.note: After говорить, думать or рассказывать, о names the topic: what someone is talking or thinking about. The noun takes the prepositional. The verb is supplied in the exercises.

teaching.title: A topic, not a location
teaching.note: This is the same case used for location after в and на, but it expresses a different relationship. Compare на работе — at work, and о работе — about work. For these nouns use -е: мама → маме, друг → друге, семья → семье, книга → книге, музыка → музыке, спорт → спорте.

teaching.title: О or об
teaching.note: Use об before the opening vowel sound in отдых: об отдыхе. The choice depends on sound, so do not replace о mechanically before every vowel letter: о языке is correct. Practise these two patterns here; pronouns such as обо мне come later.

examples.ru: Они рассказывают об отдыхе.
examples.en: They are talking about their holiday.

examples.ru: Она думает об отдыхе.
examples.en: She is thinking about taking a rest.
